head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1
changes: Decoded worker requests borrow proof bytes from the original packet; Rust lifetimes retain that packet while its proofs are consumed. Both legacy and typed requests retain their wire format and validation.

Request encoding precomputes its exact size before a fallible allocation. Request metadata and incoming typed process frames use bounded fallible exact-capacity vectors. Dependency identity uses a two-entry stack array.

Launch and artifact hashing stream the original length/domain-framed little-endian words with working storage independent of payload size. The unchanged slice hash is the independent parity reference, including at maximum protocol sizes.
Native packet pointer/capacity checks and maximum-size frame/packet/hash cases pass, along with launch fencing and typed worker lifecycle tests in both lane configurations.
Two full-size finalizers preserve the archived registry and all arithmetic-stage operation counts; input proofs remain borrowed through the GPU worker path.

selection_correction.reason: Two CPU-only lifecycle tests selected in the GPU build require the CPU reference backend. They are covered by the CPU compatibility suite; the GPU build runs its six compatible lifecycle/frame cases.

limitations: Protocol caps bound packet/frame vector capacity and per-request metadata, not complete physical RSS or enclosing scheduler admission. Coordinator copies, result serialization, verifier scratch, allocator and driver overhead still require full lifetime accounting.
Streaming hash storage is independent of payload length. Fixed permutation setup may allocate round constants; this is not a universal zero-allocation claim.

The existing decoded-proof, construction, symbolic, lookup and periodic-source allowances retain their scoped limits; arbitrary AIR/caller allocations and overlapping cached programs still require enclosing reservations.

Ordinary pool admission rejects this qualification profile without complete lifetime phases. No scheduler allowance was reduced from observed peaks. The 3 GiB worker, 4 GiB aggregate host, 7 GiB managed GPU and 1 GiB allocation caps remain enforced.
Both finalizers prove the same terminal statement through distinct verified dependencies. Their timings do not establish sustained transactions per hour or a throughput gain.
Broader transaction workloads, nonempty-child full-size merges, larger blocks, sustained pool throughput, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
